title: FIPS 140-3 Exception Registry (WO-063)
description: Schema for the structured FIPS finding exception registry at .release/fips-data/exceptions.json. Formally tracks REVIEW or FAIL findings from FIPS CI gates (or external vulnerability scanners) that have been explicitly acknowledged as an accepted risk and tracked with EXCEPTION status -- distinct from PASS/FAIL/REVIEW -- so they can be owned, justified, and re-evaluated on expiry rather than narratively documented or silently converted to PASS. Validated by tools/pipeline/internal/cmd/validate_exceptions.go (`pipeline validate-exceptions`).

finding_id.description: The identifier of the finding this exception covers -- either a FIPS quality gate check ID (e.g. FIPS-CRYPTO-002) or an external scanner ID (e.g. a Go vulnerability database ID like GO-2026-6091). A finding_id that does not match a known FIPS quality gate ID is not an error, only a warning, since it may originate from an external scanner.

original_status.description: The FIPS finding status this exception is overriding. An exception is only meaningful for a finding that was not already a clean PASS.

exception_status.description: Always EXCEPTION. An exception entry must never claim PASS (nor FAIL/REVIEW as its own status) -- see the PASS-status invariant enforced by ValidateExceptions.

owner.description: The team or individual accountable for re-evaluating this exception before it expires (e.g. security-team).

justification.description: Why this finding is being tracked as an accepted exception rather than remediated.

expiry_date.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) after which this exception must be re-evaluated. Expiry is exclusive of the date itself: an expiry_date equal to today is not yet expired.

jira_reference.description: The Jira issue tracking remediation or re-evaluation of this exception (e.g. PSP-3913).

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp this exception entry was created.
